transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good afternoon, thank you for calling S-Net technical support. My name is Marcus. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Marcus, my name is Miroslav. Since early this morning my desktop Outlook programme on my computer keeps rejecting my S-Net email password.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am really sorry for the disruption to your email this morning, Miroslav, and I completely understand how frustrating it is when your desktop mail client suddenly stops syncing.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you, Marcus. I use my s-netmail.co.uk address for all my architectural consulting correspondence, and the little password box just keeps popping back up every thirty seconds.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can imagine how distracting that constant password prompt is while you are trying to work, Miroslav. I will take full ownership of this and get your Outlook syncing properly today.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's a relief, thank you. My email is m.kowalski@s-netmail.co.uk.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Got that down. Before I open your mailbox settings, could you please verify the first line of your billing address and the answer to your security question, which is your first pet's name?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, the first line is 28 Beechwood Avenue, Sheffield, and my first pet's name is Barnaby.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Spot on, thank you for verifying those details, Miroslav. Let me ask a few quick diagnostic questions so we can pinpoint why Outlook is rejecting your login.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, go ahead.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: First, have you tried logging into your m.kowalski@s-netmail.co.uk inbox directly through a web browser on the S-Net Webmail portal today, and did that accept your password?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I tested that twenty minutes ago on Microsoft Edge! My normal password works fine in the browser and I can see new emails arriving there, just not in my desktop app.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is a very helpful clue, Miroslav. Second, which exact version of Outlook and Windows are you running on your desktop PC?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'm on Windows 11 Pro, and I use Classic Outlook 2021—not the new Windows Mail app, the proper Office 2021 desktop version.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And when the credential box pops up in Classic Outlook 2021, does it give a specific server error code at the bottom of the window, and do you know which incoming and outgoing ports you use?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It shows error 0x800CCC0E saying it cannot authenticate with imap.s-netmail.co.uk. In my Account Settings, incoming IMAP is on port 993 with SSL/TLS and outgoing SMTP is on port 465 with SSL/TLS.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that tells me everything I need. So just to recap your situation, Miroslav: your regular password logs into S-Net Webmail in Edge without any trouble.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: However, Classic Outlook 2021 on your Windows 11 PC keeps rejecting that same password on IMAP port 993 and SMTP port 465 with authentication error 0x800CCC0E since this morning.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is the exact problem, word for word.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Here is why that is happening, Miroslav. Overnight, S-Net completed a mandatory security upgrade across our @s-netmail.co.uk servers to disable basic web password authentication on third-party mail clients.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh! So Classic Outlook 2021 isn't allowed to use my normal webmail password anymore?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly right. Because Classic Outlook 2021 uses legacy IMAP authentication for custom domains, our server now requires a dedicated sixteen-character App Password instead of your main webmail password.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Ah, that makes complete sense! Why didn't the error message in Outlook just say that instead of making me think I'd forgotten my password?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely agree, Outlook's generic credential box doesn't explain why the server rejected the login, which catches a lot of people out.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, so how do we set up this sixteen-character App Password for my m.kowalski@s-netmail.co.uk mailbox?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can enable the two-factor app token generator on your mailbox from here. Just a second for me, Miroslav, I'm pulling up the legacy mail server console.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, I've got your mailbox profile open on my screen now, Miroslav, and I can see the legacy IMAP block that triggered at six o'clock this morning.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, six o'clock this morning was right before I switched my studio PC on!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Because your account had seven failed password retries from Outlook's automatic background sync, the IMAP gateway also placed a temporary thirty-minute security lock on port 993.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh dear, every time I clicked OK on that popup box in Classic Outlook 2021, I was probably making the lock worse.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Don't worry at all, Miroslav, that happens to almost everyone when the popup keeps reappearing. I have just cleared that port 993 security lock on our server for you now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wonderful, thank you for clearing that.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now I am going to provision the App Password feature on your m.kowalski@s-netmail.co.uk profile and generate a fresh sixteen-character token specifically for Classic Outlook 2021 on your Windows 11 machine.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will changing to an App Password affect how I log into S-Net Webmail on Microsoft Edge, or on my iPad?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great question, Miroslav. Your main S-Net Webmail password in Microsoft Edge stays completely unchanged—this sixteen-character token is strictly for third-party IMAP and SMTP apps.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Perfect, because I don't want to get locked out of the browser portal as well.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It won't touch your browser login at all. Hold on while I generate the sixteen-character token.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, here is the new app password ready for your Outlook client, Miroslav. I have also pushed a copy to your backup recovery SMS number ending in 419.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, my phone just buzzed with the text message from S-Net Security! I can see the sixteen-character code in four blocks of four letters.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Brilliant. When we type that into Classic Outlook 2021 on your Windows 11 PC, we need to enter all sixteen letters in lowercase with no spaces or hyphens between the blocks.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Got it, no spaces or hyphens. Where should I type it in? Should I put it straight into the little popup box or go into Account Settings?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let's put it directly into the Account Settings dialogue in Classic Outlook 2021 first, Miroslav, because that updates both incoming IMAP port 993 and outgoing SMTP port 465 at the same time.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I've got Classic Outlook 2021 open on my screen now. I'm clicking File in the top-left corner.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect. Under the Info tab, click the Account Settings button, and then select Server Settings from the drop-down menu for m.kowalski@s-netmail.co.uk.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, I've clicked Server Settings and a window has come up showing Incoming Mail at the top and Outgoing Mail underneath.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Excellent. Under Incoming Mail, where it shows imap.s-netmail.co.uk on port 993 with SSL/TLS, clear out the old password dots in the Password field.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Cleared it out. Now I'm typing the sixteen lowercase letters from the SMS message with no spaces... okay, I've typed all sixteen characters and ticked Remember password.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before you click Next, Miroslav, click on the Outgoing Mail section right below it for smtp.s-netmail.co.uk on port 465 so we make sure outgoing authentication is updated too.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Ah, good catch! Under Outgoing Mail, it has 'Use same settings as my incoming mail server' selected. Should I leave that ticked?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, leaving 'Use same settings as my incoming mail server' ticked is ideal because it automatically passes the new sixteen-character token to SMTP port 465.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And what about the checkbox that says 'Require logon using Secure Password Authentication (SPA)'? It's currently unticked.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Definitely keep SPA unticked, Miroslav—our imap.s-netmail.co.uk and smtp.s-netmail.co.uk servers use standard SSL/TLS encryption with the App Password, and ticking SPA would cause error 0x800CCC0E again.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, I'm leaving SPA unticked and clicking Next now... it says 'Account successfully updated'!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is music to my ears! Click Done on that window, and then let's hit the Send/Receive All Folders button at the top of Classic Outlook 2021 to test a live sync.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Clicking Done, and now clicking Send/Receive All Folders... look at the bottom status bar, it says 'Synchronizing subscribed folders for m.kowalski@s-netmail.co.uk'!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Fantastic! Did any credential popup window appear, or did the progress bar complete cleanly?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No popup at all! The status bar now says 'All folders are up to date' and six emails from my clients this morning just dropped straight into my Inbox.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let's also do a quick outgoing test on port 465, Miroslav. Could you send a quick test email to yourself just to confirm SMTP sending is working smoothly?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Doing that right now... typed 'Test' in the subject line to m.kowalski@s-netmail.co.uk and hit Send... it left the Outbox immediately and just arrived in my Inbox!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And on my server console I can see both the IMAP port 993 session and the SMTP port 465 dispatch authenticated cleanly with your new App Password.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Marcus, you have saved my workday. What about my iPad that I mentioned earlier? Will I need another code if the Apple Mail app asks for a password?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You can actually use that exact same sixteen-character App Password from your SMS on your iPad's Apple Mail app as well, or generate a separate one anytime inside S-Net Webmail under Security.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Where inside S-Net Webmail is that menu located, just in case I ever get a new computer?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: When you log into S-Net Webmail on Microsoft Edge, click the gear icon in the top right, select Account Security, and scroll down to App-Specific Passwords.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Gear icon, Account Security, App-Specific Passwords. I've jotted that down in my notebook next to my router details.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That way you are completely self-sufficient if you ever add another device at 28 Beechwood Avenue.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does this sixteen-character App Password ever expire after ninety days, or does it stay active permanently?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It stays active permanently on your m.kowalski@s-netmail.co.uk mailbox unless you manually revoke it inside Account Security or change your master webmail password.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's really good to know, so I won't get surprised by another popup in three months' time.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly right, Miroslav, once it is saved in Windows Credential Manager via Outlook, you won't have to touch it again.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Everything is syncing rapidly and the annoying password box hasn't come back once since we put the sixteen-character token in.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm before we wrap up, Miroslav, is your Classic Outlook 2021 email issue completely resolved to your satisfaction today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, one hundred percent resolved! Both incoming and outgoing emails are working perfectly in Outlook again.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It has been an absolute pleasure helping you get your studio email back online today, Miroslav. Thank you for choosing S-Net, and have a productive afternoon.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you very much, Marcus. Have a great afternoon too!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome, Miroslav. Do you have any other questions about your S-Net broadband or email today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, that was everything I needed. Thanks again!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you again for choosing S-Net, Miroslav. Goodbye and take care.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Bye now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.
